messages:
maya (ML Infra): Quick follow-up from the RFC meeting — we need to lock down the op boundary for quantized attention and fallback semantics.

devin (Runtime): TL;DR: propose that the Attention op owns fused dequant + matmul + softmax + out-quant steps as one kernel when input is INT8/FP8. Fallbacks should be at op level, not kernel subop. :thinking:

alicia (Eng-ML): Curious: does 'op level' fallback mean we always copy to FP16 and run the full reference path on fallback? Concerned about memory spike for long context.

devin (Runtime): Not always. Two-tier fallback: 1) local kernel fallback -> run dequant + matmul in smaller-block kernel staying quantized where possible, 2) global fallback -> materialize FP16 and call baseline. We pick based on memory budget and perf model.

samir (Platform): How does KV cache ownership work with the fused path? If we dequant inline, we change cache layout semantics. Need clear contract.

devin (Runtime): Proposal: kernel receives a CacheView that exposes get_page() returning a typed pointer plus 'format' flag (quantized|fp16). Kernel may return a CacheCommit hint describing if cache was mutated and in what format. Platform layer enforces format compatibility.

maya (ML Infra): Could we use a 'lazy dequant' handle where the kernel keeps KV in quantized memory and only materializes a small window to FP16 for softmax, avoiding full copy? That would help long contexts.

alicia (Eng-ML): Lazy dequantism sounds good but we need deterministic rounding and reproducible RNG behavior for attention dropout. That must be identical across quant/FP paths.

devin (Runtime): Agreed — RNG seeds must be derived from request ID + position, independent of whether we took fallback. Add a conformance test.

maya (ML Infra): Another practical detail: in-place dequant to shared scratch can race across batches in the same worker. We should make scratch per-request or use locks; both have cost. Thoughts?

devin (Runtime): Prefer per-request scratch when possible. For high-throughput shared workers we offer pooling with epoch tokens to avoid locks. Will add to design doc.

samir (Platform): What about metrics? We need per-op breakdown: tokens served via fused-quant kernel, tokens via local fallback, tokens via global fallback, avg latency delta. Ops team will surf dashboards for rollouts.

maya (ML Infra): Add an eval script to run a test matrix: batch sizes [1,8,64], seq len [128,512,2048], models [gpt-like 7B, 13B], dtype [FP16, FP8-ym, INT8]. Capture memory, p99 latency and perplexity diff on 1k prompts.

alicia (Eng-ML): For correctness, include nans/inf detection in quant kernels. If scaling fails, signal a kernel-level error and escalate to global fallback.

devin (Runtime): Implementation notes: new KernelCapability flags: supports_fused_attention, supports_lazy_dequant, cache_format_compat. Kernel registry will pick highest-priority kernel that satisfies all flags for the request policy (latency-first vs cost-first).

maya (ML Infra): One more: rollout plan — start with canary pinned to a small fleet, compare cost and quality metrics, enable auto-fallback if regressions exceed thresholds.

runtime-bot: Canary deploy scheduled: cluster=canary-quant-01, start=2026-04-02T02:00:00Z.

devin (Runtime): I'll draft the follow-up RFC with the op contract, CacheView API, KernelCapability bits, and the test matrix. Assigning to @maya and @alicia for perf and correctness sections.

maya (ML Infra): Thanks — I'll add perf knobs and the eval harness.

alicia (Eng-ML): I'll own the ML regression tests and RNG determinism checks.

samir (Platform): I'll wire metrics and rollout automation.

devin (Runtime): Great. Next sync Friday to review the RFC draft. :+1:
